result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both emails are about 67–73 words and keep every required fact: the March 3 date, the booking link, the walk-in caveat, the new hours and the unchanged $85 price. A's email is clean and needs no edits, but B goes past the rubric's one-line limit on notes. B's extra note correctly points out that March 3 isn't a Monday in 2026 or 2027, which could stop a wrong date going to the whole customer list. That outweighs B's extra length and its rubric penalty. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both edits come in well under 90 words (about 68 for A and 72 for B) and keep every required fact without adding anything new. B is the cleaner ready-to-send version, while A goes past the one-line note limit. A wins because it catches a real error before the email reaches every customer: March 3 is a Tuesday in 2026 (and a Wednesday in 2027), so 'Monday, March 3' is wrong.
